chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Musa ibn 'Umar, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Ansari, from al-Husayn ibn Zayd, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon them both), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Regarding a stray animal that a man finds, if he intends to take a fee (reward) for it and it perishes, he is liable (for its value); and if he did not intend to take a fee for it and it perished, there is no liability upon him.'

key_terms.جُعْلًا: A fee or reward for service

ai.seo_question: What is the liability of a person who finds and keeps a stray animal if it dies?
ai.summary: Transmitted through the chain of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq from Imam Ali, this hadith clarifies the principle of liability (dhaman) in custodianship (hiyazah) by linking it to the finder's intention (niyyah). It establishes that assuming a reward creates a contractual obligation for the animal's safety, whereas gratuitous care exempts the finder from liability for accidental death, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on intent in civil transactions.
